title: Rescuing the One Who Wronged You

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: A man who had escaped came and reported this to Abram the Hebrew... When Abram heard that his relative had been taken captive, he called out the 318 trained men born in his household and went in pursuit as far as Dan. - Gen 14:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Consider what Abram had every right to feel. Lot had taken the best land, walked away from him, and settled in a wicked city. This was the natural consequence of Lot's own choices. Abram could easily have said, "He made his bed; let him lie in it."

Instead, the moment Abram hears, he acts. He arms 318 men and rides out to war for the nephew who had wronged him. No lecture, no "I told you so," no hesitation. Just rescue.

This is the mark of a heart shaped by God. Abram doesn't wait for Lot to deserve help. He doesn't calculate whether Lot has earned it. Love simply moves toward the one in trouble.

And is this not exactly what God has done for us? "While we were still sinners, Christ died for us" (Rom 5:8). We had wandered off by our own choice, made our own bed in a far country - and He came for us anyway. Jesus taught us to love even those who wrong us (Luke 6:35), and He showed us how. Is there someone whose trouble is their own fault, whom God is calling you to help anyway? Grace doesn't wait for people to deserve it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there someone in trouble by their own fault whom God calls you to help?
- Do you wait for people to deserve your grace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You came for me when my trouble was my own fault. Give me a heart like that - quick to help, slow to say "I told you so." Let grace move me toward those who need rescue.
Amen.
